answer: Written in a numbers heavy, no adjectives register, it stays short. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on cost-of-replication accounting, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. A umber of per-task receipts records who did what, and the bridge of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. Reaching the cipher of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys.
